scope: Proposition 5.7 of the manuscript “The maximum number of mutually unbiased bases in dimension six” (preprints/The-maximum-number-of-mutually-unbiased-bases-in-dimension-six-September-24-2026/The-maximum-number-of-mutually-unbiased-bases-in-dimension-six-September-24-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 266 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 b4cc74c840c90249), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 38. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Suppose Stage B is run on a finite list of records with valid Root certificates, under the arithmetic assumptions and error bounds of Section A. On a completed run, let A be its final atlas of children and let B be the list of input parents whose refinement failed. Then ⋃︂ (P,R) input S(P, R) ⊆ ⋃︂ (Q,r)∈A S(Q, r) ∪ ⋃︂ (P,R)∈B S(P, R). (5.26) In particular, a completed run with no bad parents replaces the input cover by a child cover. A nonempty bad list remains an obligation.
